definition: Identify affairs whose substantive policy subject is digitalisation. Include digital public services, e-government, electronic identity and procedures, government IT and cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, data protection and digital rights, digital media and platforms, broadband and digital connectivity. Include these subjects in any sector, not only public administration. Exclude affairs that merely mention a website, email, electronic document, or routine IT tool; exclude general administration, conventional broadcasting, postal services, and physical infrastructure unless a substantive digital-policy issue is established. Judge the target affair, not unrelated items in attached meeting minutes. Missing substantive evidence means insufficient evidence, not a negative.

limitations: Human editorial positive references, not complete binary ground truth. Unlisted affairs are unlabelled, not negative.
DVS and PolitMonitor overlap; additional sample excludes every DVS ID. They are not independent label sources.
This estimates recovery of curated positives, not discovery precision or full-corpus recall.
Missing sources, invalid evidence, abstentions and API errors remain in the completed-run denominator.
Keyword baseline uses titles in the selected language; Apertus uses title and fetched source content.
DVS cohort is skewed toward German. Additional language samples are small and not representative.
Reference labels and membership are never passed to the inference request.
